findings.description: Ruby before 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10 has a heap-based buffer overflow during case conversion. One byte can be written outside a buffer for, for example, ISO-8859-1 or Windows-1252.

The Comelit 1456B Multi-User Gateway, in firmware versions up to and including 2.10.0, allows a user authenticated to the web interface with the Installer role to export a system configuration backup. The resulting backup file contains the configured passwords for all privileged roles

Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Reconciliation Manage).   The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.2 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N).

The Comelit 1456B Multi-User Gateway, in firmware versions up to and including 2.10.0, is configured with static default passwords for multiple privileged roles. None of these passwords are required to be changed during initial configuration, and they remain at their default values unless the administrator changes them manually. An attacker with network access to the device can authenticate using these default credentials and gain administrative control.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

The WPO365 | SEAMLESS WORDPRESS + MICROSOFT INTEGRATION (WPO365 | LOGIN) WordPress plugin before 45.4 does not ensure the signature validated on a SAML response covers the element the user identity is read from, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a response via signature wrapping and log in as any user, including administrators, when they can supply a single artifact signed by the configured identity provider.

The AppPresser  WordPress plugin before 5.0.0 does not properly escape the contents of its debug log when displaying it in the admin dashboard, and decodes escape sequences after sanitising input, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored XSS attacks against administrators when debug logging is enabled.

The SAML SSO Login  WordPress plugin through 1.5.2 does not verify that the SAML assertion whose signature it validates is the same assertion it reads the user identity from, allowing unauthenticated attackers who hold a validly signed assertion for any identity to authenticate as any existing user, including an administrator, through XML signature wrapping.

Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:ulabel/1 in src/idna.erl hands every ASCII label that starts with xn-- to punycode:decode/1 without applying check_label_length/1, the 63-octet DNS label limit. punycode:decode/1 in src/punycode.erl builds its output with list appends in insert/4, so its cost grows super-linearly with the label length. A label of a few kilobytes keeps a scheduler busy for seconds to minutes before the label is rejected as invalid punycode.

Every decode entry point reaches this path: decode/1, decode/2, to_unicode/1 and from_ascii/1. The encode path reaches it as well, because alabel/1 calls ulabel/1 on an ASCII xn-- label before its own length check, so encode/1, encode/2 and to_ascii/1 are affected for such input.

This issue affects idna: from 0.5.0 before 8.0.0.

The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

A malicious actor with access to the network could exploit a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability found in UniFi Access Application to obtain information and make unauthorized changes on the host device.

A flaw was found in nbdkit. The qcow2dec filter's zstd_compressed_cluster() function incorrectly sets the ZSTD input buffer size to the uncompressed cluster size instead of the compressed buffer size. A crafted QCOW2 image with ZSTD-compressed clusters can trigger a heap over-read, leading to a denial of service and potentially exposing heap memory.

A security flaw has been discovered in SourceCodester E-Commerce Shopping Cart Web Application 1.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file action.php. The manipulation of the argument keyword results in sql injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When a task or its parameters are marked no_log: true, sensitive values passed to a module's warn() or deprecate() calls are not redacted and are printed in cleartext to stdout/stderr in warning and deprecation messages. The 'warnings' and 'deprecations' keys are retained in the PRESERVE allow-list in lib/ansible/_internal/_task.py when the task result is censored, so sensitive parameters bypass masking and can be disclosed in output captured in terminal sessions, CI logs, and any automation wrapping ansible-playbook, even though every task touching the secrets is marked no_log: true.

A flaw has been found in SEO Panel 6.0.0. Affected is an unknown function of the file controllers/siteauditor.ctrl.php of the component Site Auditor. Executing a manipulation of the argument order_col/order_val can lead to sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 7.0.0 is able to address this issue. This patch is called 2a2d4aeb718177327b0cd8ce17e2f40328772127. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.

The NextScripts: Social Networks Auto-Poster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'comment_author' and 'comment_agent' Comment Fields in all versions up to, and including, 4.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload executes in an administrator's browser session when the administrator views the WordPress comment moderation queue, including pending and unapproved comments, meaning no prior approval of the comment is required for exploitation.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Public News Article Rendering Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows authenticated attackers with administrative or sub-administrative privileges to inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript through the postdescription parameter when creating or editing news articles. The application renders the stored post content without proper output encoding in news-details.php, allowing injected JavaScript to execute in the browsers of users who visit the affected article.

A Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The $currenturl variable in news-details.php is constructed using unencoded REQUEST_URI and HTTP_HOST server variables and echoed directly into the href attributes of social share links. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by crafting a URL containing HTML metacharacters to break out of the href attribute and execute arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the context of the victim's browser.

An Unrestricted File Upload vulnerability in the admin panel of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1 allows authenticated attackers to upload files with arbitrary content by bypassing weak filename extension validation in add-post.php and change-image.php. Although files are renamed with an image extension upon storage, the lack of MIME type and content validation enables content spoofing, storage of malicious markup, and creates a vector for Remote Code Execution (RCE) with server misconfigurations or secondary Local File Inclusion.

A Session Fixation vulnerability exists in the admin login endpoint (/admin/index.php) of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The application fails to regenerate the session identifier (PHPSESSID) upon successful authentication. A remote attacker can exploit this by setting a known session ID in the victim's browser prior to login. Once the victim authenticates, the attacker can reuse the fixed session ID to hijack the victim's authenticated session.
An issue in PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System (ELMS) Version 2.1 allows a remote attacker to escalate privileges via the PHP session management mechanism
An issue in PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System (ELMS) Version 2.1 allows a remote attacker to escalate privileges via the password recovery functionality

PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V1.1 uses a non-cryptographic function to generate security-sensitive appointment and invoice identifiers. The identifiers are generated within a restricted numeric range and are subsequently used in record lookup operations. This implementation exposes the application to identifier prediction or guessing attacks under conditions where the identifiers are relied upon as a security boundary.
PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V 1.1 is vulnerable to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in admin/search-invoices.php via the searchdata parameter.

PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System v2.1 contains an insufficient verification vulnerability in the password recovery functionality in forgot-password.php. The application allows an unauthenticated user to access the password-change workflow by providing a valid employee ID and corresponding email address without requiring an additional out-of-band verification mechanism.

PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System V2.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because database backup files are stored within the publicly accessible web root. An unauthenticated remote attacker can download the SQL backup files and retrieve sensitive database contents, including employee personally identifiable information and password hashes.

An insecure password reset vulnerability in the Admin Password Recovery Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to change an administrator or sub-administrator account password by providing the corresponding username and email address. The application does not require verification of account ownership through an email token, OTP, or another authentication mechanism before updating the password, potentially resulting in account takeover.

A Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the admin panel of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1 allows remote attackers to hijack the authentication of administrators and perform unauthorized state-changing actions, such as adding, editing, or deleting posts and sub-admins, or changing passwords, via crafted HTTP requests. This occurs because the application fails to implement anti-CSRF tokens for admin actions and permits destructive operations via HTTP GET requests.
